correctness.rationale: This pass applies to repairs/2/RESULT.md, not the frozen wording. As written over all n, the original's positive-limit premise is unattainable: it forces u_n-b_n to converge for b_n=log_2 n+log_2 log_2 n, whereas b_n has distinct lattice phases, and the original applies its theorem along subsequences anyway. The corrected theorem explicitly quantifies over arbitrary sequences of sizes tending to infinity, retains full-sequence tightness, fixes integer rounding in the coordinate truncation, and proves nonconvergence using sizes 2^(2^t) and floor(2^(2^t+1/2)). Rechecked the repaired claim: counts by length are squared positive-composition binomials, giving the stated hypergeometric law and an exponentially negligible noncentral contribution even to fixed factorial moments. In the central range the exact stars-and-bars ratio for O(log n) total size is uniformly the product of positive geometric(1/2) probabilities times 1+o(1). The coordinate tail bound with floor(T/2) makes the discarded part o(n^(-r)) for each fixed order r. The exact geometric-sum tail u*2^(1-u) times the asymptotic step count n/2 gives the stated intensity. Exchangeability, factorial moments, and moment determinacy give Poisson limits along each phase; rank events are the corresponding count events. Compactness of the intensities at rounded offsets gives tightness over all sizes; the two phases give different centered CDF values at every offset in (0,1/2). The original finite checker was inspected, not executed; it checks finite paths, not the limiting argument.
